- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.

- review: Review a pull request

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "#!/bin/bash
# exp-020: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct FOLIO full (204 problems)
# Powered replication of exp-011 FOLIO signal (+10pp, SICA 70% vs SC 60%)
# exp-011 used 30 FOLIO (underpowered); this uses full 204 for statistical power
# K=12, T=0.7, max-tokens=4096, seed=42
set -e
cd /root/symb_invariant_consensus
source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base

MODEL="/root/autodl-tmp/models/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct/LLM-Research/Meta-Llama-3___1-8B-Instruct"
PORT=8000
RESULTS_DIR="results/exp020_llama8b_folio204"
mkdir -p "$RESULTS_DIR"

echo "=== exp-020: LLaMA-8B FOLIO Full (204 problems) ==="
echo "Start: $(date)"

# Clean up ANY existing vLLM processes
echo "Cleaning up any existing vLLM processes..."
pkill -9 -f "vllm.entrypoints" 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 5
echo "GPU status after cleanup:"
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv,noheader

# Step 1: Start vLLM (LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct)
echo "=== [$(date)] Starting vLLM (LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct) on port $PORT ==="
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --model "$MODEL" \
    --max-model-len 8192 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --port $PORT \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype auto > /tmp/vllm_exp020.log 2>&1 &
VLLM_PID=$!
echo "vLLM PID: $VLLM_PID"

# Step 2: Wait for vLLM ready (up to 180s)
echo "Waiting for vLLM to be ready..."
for i in $(seq 1 180); do
    if curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "vLLM ready after ${i}s"
        break
    fi
    if ! kill -0 $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "ERROR: vLLM process died. Check /tmp/vllm_exp020.log"
        tail -20 /tmp/vllm_exp020.log
        exit 1
    fi
    sleep 1
done

if ! curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: vLLM did not start within 180s"
    kill $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null
    exit 1
fi

# Step 3: Run SICA vs SC on full FOLIO (204 problems)
echo "=== [$(date)] Running exp-020: FOLIO full, K=12, T=0.7, 204 problems ==="
python3 run_full_mvp.py \
    --mode vllm \
    --k 12 \
    --temperature 0.7 \
    --max-tokens 4096 \
    --api-base "http://localhost:$PORT/v1" \
    --model auto \
    --math-data data/empty.json \
    --no-proofwriter \
    --folio-data data/folio_full.json \
    --output "$RESULTS_DIR/exp020_results.json" \
    --save-intermediates \
    --seed 42

EXIT_CODE=$?

# Step 4: Cleanup
echo "=== [$(date)] Stopping vLLM ==="
kill $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null || true
wait $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null || true
echo "End: $(date)"
echo "EXIT_CODE=$EXIT_CODE"
echo "EXP020_DONE"

{"success": true, "data": {"stdout": "#!/bin/bash
# exp-011: LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct SICA evaluation (cross-family validation)
# D012: 30 FOLIO + 30 ProofWriter D5, K=12, T=0.7, max_tokens=8192
# Claim 2 cross-model-family validation (non-Qwen architecture)
set -e
cd /root/symb_invariant_consensus
source /root/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh && conda activate base

MODEL="/root/autodl-tmp/models/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct/LLM-Research/Meta-Llama-3___1-8B-Instruct"
PORT=8002
RESULTS_DIR="results/exp011_llama8b"
mkdir -p "$RESULTS_DIR"

# Clean up ANY existing vLLM processes (e.g. residual Qwen-14B occupying GPU)
echo "Cleaning up any existing vLLM processes..."
pkill -9 -f "vllm.entrypoints" 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 5
# Verify GPU is freed
echo "GPU status after cleanup:"
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used --format=csv,noheader

# Step 1: Start vLLM in background
echo "=== [$(date)] Starting vLLM (LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct) on port $PORT ==="
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
    --model "$MODEL" \
    --max-model-len 8192 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
    --port $PORT \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dtype auto > /tmp/vllm_exp011.log 2>&1 &
VLLM_PID=$!
echo "vLLM PID: $VLLM_PID"

# Step 2: Wait for vLLM ready (up to 180s)
echo "Waiting for vLLM to be ready..."
for i in $(seq 1 180); do
    if curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "vLLM ready after ${i}s"
        break
    fi
    if ! kill -0 $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "ERROR: vLLM process died. Check /tmp/vllm_exp011.log"
        cat /tmp/vllm_exp011.log | tail -20
        exit 1
    fi
    sleep 1
done

if ! curl -s http://localhost:$PORT/v1/models > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "ERROR: vLLM did not start within 180s"
    kill $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null
    exit 1
fi

# Step 3: Run SICA pipeline
echo "=== [$(date)] Running SICA pipeline: K=12, T=0.7, 60 problems ==="
python3 run_full_mvp.py \
    --mode vllm \
    --k 12 \
    --temperature 0.7 \
    --max-tokens 4096 \
    --api-base "http://localhost:$PORT/v1" \
    --math-data data/empty.json \
    --pw-data data/proofwriter_30.json \
    --folio-data data/folio_30.json \
    --output "$RESULTS_DIR/exp011_results.json" \
    --save-intermediates \
    --seed 42

# Step 4: Cleanup
echo "=== [$(date)] Stopping vLLM ==="
kill $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null || true
wait $VLLM_PID 2>/dev/null || true
echo "EXP011_DONE"
